title: Two cipher letters to J. G. von Ilten, London, Feb-Mar 1743, GWLB Hannover Ms XXIII 1234:29,2

documents.route: unsigned (London) to J. G. von Ilten

plaintext.source: none: no decipherment on or with the letter

transcription.source: GWLB Kitodo master images (public domain), read in crops
transcription.notes: German clear opening and close; 25 lines of numeric code with no decipherment; a few end digits in the gutter, read from a full-resolution crop (75? unresolved).

documents.route: Ernst von Steinberg (London) to J. G. von Ilten

plaintext.source: contemporary decipherment in the recipient's office

transcription.source: GWLB Kitodo master images (public domain), read in crops
transcription.notes: German letter with three French code runs; p. 121 is a contemporary worksheet glossing the groups, partly wrongly.

system.summary: Hanoverian French syllabic nomenclator of 863 numbered groups (blanks and 864-1000 are nulls), with homophones, officers' and place names, and control groups 'annulle' / 'repete la precedente'.
system.notes: Two-part code: numbered decoding table (pp. 390-391) and alphabetical encoding table (pp. 386-388) in Ms XXIII 1234:31,1. 172 'Duc' is used for 'du'.

prior_solution.where: Letter 2 only: a contemporary worksheet (p. 121) glossing its 34 groups, with errors and a skipped pair. Letter 1: none.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and posed the problem with /goal, pasting the catalogue entry. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: two transcription subagents for the key table

solution.what: While checking catalogue 346, fetched the two 1743 Ilten letters flagged 'Teilweise dechiffrierter Brief' (Ms XXIII 1234:29,2) from GWLB Kitodo.
Transcribed letter 1's 189 code groups (no decipherment on it) and letter 2's 34 groups with the p. 121 worksheet glosses.
Kalliope search 'Ilten Chiffre*': volume 1234:31,1 (1745/46) lists a 'Chiffre-Tabelle', pp. 386-391.
Fetched pp. 386-391: numbered decoding table 1-863 and alphabetical encoding table; transcribed the decoding side (two agents, 28 checks against the worksheet values).
Applied the table to letter 1: fluent French on forage and discipline, Du Pontpietin and Sommerfeldt; dateline 866.223 = [null] Londres.
Applied it to letter 2: the worksheet's values agree group for group; the key also restores 278.613 'quoique avec' and corrects 'in-tra-c-tion' to 'instruction'.
Re-read the gutter digits from a full-resolution crop: 51, 407, 59, 95, 70, 705 ('ce dernier point'); 75? stays open.

outcome.method: read after matching with key from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The key table sits in a different volume of the Ilten papers (Ms XXIII 1234:31,1, 1745/46); it was found through the catalogue and matched to the 1743 letters by the worksheet values of letter 2.
outcome.fraction_read_source: ciphertext_feb26.txt + ciphertext_mar29.txt: 223 code groups; not reading as sense: 283, 75?, 59 in letter 1

gaps.item: letter 1 p. 74: 283.75? before 'me' (last digit in the gutter)

outcome.notes: Letter 1 had no decipherment at all; letter 2's contemporary worksheet was incomplete and partly wrong.
